{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use Spring XD module framework conventions (source/sink) for the new load generator and sink modules.",
    "Build the EC2 AMI on a recent Amazon Linux base, using Packer (or equivalent automation) for reproducibility.",
    "Reuse the existing Kafka client library and Spring XD Kafka source module to fix offset management.",
    "Extend the existing Jenkins-based CI infrastructure to schedule Windows agents; do not introduce a new CI tool.",
    "Use Jekyll (the GitHub Pages default) with the existing Spring XD theme for the static documentation site.",
    "Model the pluggable SPI after the Cloud Foundry Diego/Lattice runtime concepts to enable pluggable deployment targets.",
    "Design the load sink to compute throughput using tumbling time windows with counters, not per-message timestamps, to minimize overhead during perf tests.",
    "Fix Kafka offset management by switching to explicit offset commits per batch and persisting offsets in the XD container's offset store.",
    "Scope the Lattice/Diego POC as a design spike producing a written report and a minimal reference implementation, not a production feature."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Java 8 is the development language, consistent with the Spring XD timeframe.",
    "The developer has access to the AWS account used by the XD project and the necessary permissions to create AMIs.",
    "An existing CI infrastructure (e.g., Jenkins master) is available and can be extended with Windows build agents.",
    "A reachable Kafka cluster is available for the AMI, modules, and perf tests.",
    "Performance testing tooling (e.g., JMH or in-house load driver) is available or will be developed as part of the load generator module.",
    "GitHub Pages is provisioned for the repository; no new hosting decision is required.",
    "Cloud Foundry Diego/Lattice documentation and an available environment exist for the POC.",
    "All activities are performed by a single experienced developer familiar with Spring XD, Kafka, and AWS.",
    "Effort estimates cover design, implementation, unit/integration tests, and basic documentation per activity; no large separate QA or release-management effort is included.",
    "Existing test failures on Windows are assumed to be limited in scope (a handful of fixes) rather than systemic architectural issues."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "EC2 AMI for Kafka Performance Tests",
      "activity_description": "Design, build, and validate an EC2 AMI that includes the JDK, Kafka client/server, and required performance testing packages so that Kafka perf tests can be run reproducibly on EC2 instances.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Load Generator Source Module",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a new Spring XD source module that generates configurable synthetic load (rate, payload size, message format) for performance testing, including unit and integration tests and module documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Load Receiving Sink Module",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a new Spring XD sink module that receives messages and measures received throughput using windowed counters, including unit and integration tests and module documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Windows CI Build Scheduling and Test Stabilization",
      "activity_description": "Provision Windows build agents, configure CI jobs to run XD runtime tests on Windows, investigate remaining test failures, fix or isolate them, and document the resulting stable Windows build configuration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Fix Kafka Source Offset Management",
      "activity_description": "Analyze the current Kafka source offset handling, redesign it for efficient batched fetch operations from given offsets, implement the fix, add regression tests, and update module documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Performance Numbers for a Simple Stream",
      "activity_description": "Set up a benchmark environment using the new AMI and modules, run a simple stream workload, measure overall throughput, analyze the results, and publish the numbers in a short performance report.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Static GitHub Pages Site for XD Collateral",
      "activity_description": "Design the information architecture, create Jekyll-based pages, and organize samples, tutorials, links, performance benchmarks, and reference architectures so that new users can quickly get up and running on XD.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Lattice/Diego Pluggable SPI POC",
      "activity_description": "Continue the Lattice/Diego proof of concept: research the Diego runtime, design a pluggable SPI for the XD runtime, build a minimal reference implementation, and document scope, risks, and overall design for the SPI.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 236
  }
}
```
